decisions.reason: As a location-based analytics product with its own page, it fits the firm's existing software and data capabilities closely enough that management is likely to keep learning from early use and refine it rather than withdraw it.

A gas tariff comparison tool builds on the firm's related knowledge in tariff data and location-based software, and the dedicated page suggests enough commitment to continue improving it despite some overlap risk with broader tariff products.
The regional electricity tariff calculator is close to the firm's established programming and comparison-tool knowledge base, so absorptive capacity is high and supports continued commercialization.

Because this broader regional energy tariff calculator was only mentioned on the website and overlaps with more clearly presented specialist products, management would be relatively likely to consolidate and drop it.

The regional area definition tool appears strongly aligned with the firm's core geospatial and software competences, making it a useful capability-building product that management is likely to retain.

This site-specific energy tariff comparison product was only mentioned rather than fully presented and seems redundant with the firm's other tariff comparison offerings, increasing the chance of withdrawal.
